The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant/s - original claimant/s - legal heirs of the deceased - Madansinh Motisinh Rathod, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the common judgment and award dated 20.09.2006 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Ahmedabad (Rural) in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1094 of 1996, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.5,76,900/- with 7.5% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding Opponents No.2 and 3 i.e. owner and insurance company of the Truck bearing registration No.GJ-1-T-5810 liable, jointly and severally.

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 That on 31.03.1996 at about 6:15 p.m., deceased - Madansinh, along with other persons, was travelling in the Jeep bearing registration No.RJ-12-C-0291 and going from Dhandhuka to Ahmedabad and opponent No.4 - Faridkhan (Haridkhan), who was deleted later on before the Tribunal, was driving the said jeep on the correct side of the road and in a moderate speed and when they were passing near Haripura Patiya on Bagodara Road, at that time, the Truck bearing registration No.GJ-1-T-5810 being driven by opponent No.1 in full speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/64/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined from opposite side and dashed with the Jeep.
As a result, the deceased sustained serious injuries and ultimately, the deceased succumbed to the injuries.

Therefore, the legal heirs of the deceased i.e. widow and two children and mother (mother was not in the appeal proceeding) have filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.11 lakhs with cost and interest for unnatural and untimely death against the present respondents before the Tribunal.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponents No.1, 2 and 5 i.e. driver and owner of the Truck and owner of the Jeep, have chosen not to appear and contest the claim petition before the Tribunal.
Opponent No.4 was deleted before the Tribunal.

Opponent No.3 & 6 - Insurance Company of the Truck and Jeep, respectively, have appeared and filed their written statements / objections, by disputing all the averments made by the claimant in the claim petition.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.

After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding Ugamlkuvar Wd/O Madansinh Motisinh ... vs Rameshbhai Popatbhai Suvaniya ... on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188564096/

Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the present appeal is preferred by the claimant/s for enhancement.
3.1 Learned advocate for the appellant/s - claimant/s has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not properly calculating the amount of compensation.

He has submitted that amount of award is on lower side as the Tribunal has not properly considered the various aspects; like prospective income of the deceased, negligence, liability and family circumstances, etc.
He has submitted that the deceased was aged about only 45 years at the time of accident and was serving as Fitter in Simalwada Taluka Panchayat.

He has submitted that at the relevant point of time, his monthly income was Rs.5,370/-
as per the documentary evidence produced at Exh.86.

He has submitted that the learned Tribunal has not considered the prospective income, deduction of personal expenses looking to the age of the deceased and multiplier in view of the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court.

In support of his submissions, he has relied upon the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of (i) National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Shethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 and Sarla Verma versus Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.

He has NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/64/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined submitted that therefore, considering the loss of dependency, it would be calculated as Rs.5,370/- as monthly income plus 30%
prospective income minus 1/4th as personal expenses multiplied by 12 months and multiplied by 14 multiplier would come the total loss of dependency, which should be awarded to the claimants by the learned Tribunal.

3.2 He has further submitted that considering the general and non-pecuniary damages, the learned Tribunal should award Rs.18,150/- each, towards loss of estate and funeral expenses in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Shethi (supra).

He has also submitted that towards loss of consortium, there are four claimants originally before the Tribunal and therefore, it would be awarded Rs.48,400/- to each claimant as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @
Satwinder Kaur reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780.

He has submitted that the amount under the head of loss of consortium is just and proper.
He has submitted that this appeal may be dismissed and no interference be made by this Court.
4.2 Ms. Hina Desai, learned advocate for respondent No.6 - Insurance Company has submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper.
She has submitted that the Tribunal has not passed any adverse order against respondent No.6 - insurance company.
She has submitted that appropriate order may be passed.

It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/64/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.
It also endeavors to make good the human suffering to the extent possible and to also save families which have lost their breadwinners from being pushed to wandering.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
6.1 I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
From the record, it transpires that the deceased was aged about 45 years and was serving as Fitter in Simalwada Taluka Panchayat.

He has submitted that at the relevant point of time, his monthly income was Rs.5,370/- as per the documentary evidence produced at Exh.86 and his monthly income was Rs.5,370/- at the relevant point of time.
Therefore, it should be considered as monthly income of the deceased.

Hence, it would come to Rs.5,370/- per month and by adding 30%
prospective income, as not calculated by the learned Tribunal, it would come to Rs.1,611/- and therefore, total income comes to Rs.6,981/- per month.

Since the deceased is aged about 45 years and there NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/64/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined are four dependents / original claimants, 1/4th would be proper to be deducted as personal expenses and therefore, it would come to Rs.1,745/-.

Hence, the income would come to Rs.5,236/- per month and therefore, yearly, it would come to Rs.62,832/- and applying 14 multiplier as per the schedule of the Motor Vehicles Act as well as the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma versus Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121

6.2 Further, considering the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Shethi (supra), as general and non-pecuniary damages, under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, if we award Rs.18,150/- and Rs.18,150/-, respectively, which would be the just and proper compensation.

6.3 Further, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co.
Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780, Rs.40,000/-
consortium to each original claimant / dependent and 10% rise, which comes to Rs.48,400/- as consortium to each original claimant / dependent, which should be awarded to the claimants.

8.1 The appeal is partly allowed.

8.2 Respondent No.3 - Insurance Company is directed NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/64/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined to deposit the entire awarded amount, if yet not deposited, including the enhanced amount, as noted above, with interest and cost as decided by the Tribunal, from the date of claim petition till its realisation, before the concerned Tribunal, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.

in accordance with rules/law.
